mechanism_claim: The apparent industry-allocation advantage is not an industry effect; it is a proxy for a momentum-stage/regime factor that the IBD-style B0 selection already concentrates on, but does not adequately filter. Industry tag is downstream of the underlying features (mom_20, up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, px_vs_ma50, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct, ma10_slope_5) that actually differentiate winners from ruins and false negatives in the failure archaeology. Any marginal return attributed to 'industry' should vanish once those features are properly controlled or matched.
evidence_for: The largest standardized deltas separating false_negative_relative from selected_winner are feature deltas, not industry: up_day_ratio_20 (-1.19σ, median 0.50 vs 0.625), vol_ratio_5_20 (-1.05σ, 1.179 vs 1.424), mom_20 (-1.00σ, 0.058 vs 0.163), px_vs_ma50 (-0.85σ, 0.056 vs 0.127). These are momentum/quality signals, not sector labels.

Selected_winner and false_positive_ruin cases share 'extended late-stage entry' signatures that are sector-agnostic: e.g., entity_6618d3e80c (winner) and entity_4fdc3699fd (ruin) both have ma10_slope_5 ~ 0.075–0.090 and px_vs_ma50 > 0.10; entity_b6bcccdf6a (ruin) and entity_2c58cebc59 (winner) both have ma10_slope_5 in 0.013–0.067 and strong mom_20. The discriminator is not industry — it is entry tightness and momentum maturity.

Pullback features (pullback_duration_weeks median 5.5 vs 4.0; pullback_pct -15.9 vs -7.3) differentiate winners from false negatives but are stock-specific base characteristics, not industry-typical. Industry cannot explain why one stock with a deeper, longer base works and another does not.

Cases cluster by snapshot_anon (e.g., snap_71486ed83c contributes 6 of 27 archaeology rows, snap_d0d57b1e40 contributes 4). Snapshot-tagged clustering is consistent with a regime/timing explanation rather than a structural industry explanation.

B0 selection (is_b0_pick=true) is itself a filter that, by construction, over-samples names in momentum-confirmed leadership; leadership names cluster in 1–3 sectors per regime, so any portfolio factor correlated with leadership will look like an industry effect.

False positives with steep ma10_slope_5 and high ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct (e.g., entity_8f0df3d38e: ma10_slope_5=0.054, ibd_entry gap=6.85%; entity_84824e6a20: ma10_slope_5=0.062, gap=7.38%) are textbook 'buying the 8th inning of momentum' failures — a timing failure mode that operates identically across sectors.
evidence_against: The numeric_contrasts table is truncated, so I cannot verify whether any sector-level feature was even recorded or tested in this archaeology; the case-level features available are all sector-agnostic, which is silent rather than disconfirming on industry per se.

It is possible (not demonstrated in this evidence) that certain industries systematically exhibit different distributions of the discriminating features (e.g., biotech having lower up_day_ratio_20), in which case 'industry' would be a valid coarse-grained feature even if reducible to its constituents — falsification must come from the matched-pair test below, not from armchair reasoning.

The 11 selected_winners include some with extreme strength (entity_ead73f4390: mom_20=0.32, px_vs_ma50=0.185) that could in principle be sector-tagged in ways the truncated feature table hides; the visible evidence is consistent with but does not exhaust the possibility of an industry residual.

Snapshot concentration could alternatively indicate a structural shift in industry leadership that was correctly captured, rather than a regime artifact — distinguishing these requires the time-stability test, which the frozen evidence does not contain.
falsifiable_predictions: Matched-pair sector test: within a (mom_20 quintile × vol_ratio_5_20 quintile × ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct quintile × up_day_ratio_20 quintile) bucket, the W4 return difference between B0-pick industry A and B0-pick industry B will have |t| < 1.0 and a sign inconsistent across buckets. If industry is the true driver, the sign should be stable across buckets.

Sector HHI of B0 winners minus sector HHI of B0 ruins should be near zero in any single snapshot_anon bucket; the cross-snapshot variation in sector concentration will explain more W4 return variance than any sector dummy in a within-snapshot regression.

Adding sector fixed effects to a regression of W4 return on (mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, px_vs_ma50, up_day_ratio_20, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct, ma10_slope_5) will increase adjusted R^2 by less than 2 percentage points; without the features, sector dummies will look powerful (the trap to avoid).

A sector-neutralized portfolio that matches each B0 winner on (mom_20, vol_ratio_5_20, up_day_ratio_20) will retain ≥ 80% of the un-neutralized W4 alpha, and the residual 20% will be concentrated in 1–2 calendar quarters rather than spread across the sample.

Replacing the 'industry tilt' with a 'momentum-stage penalty' rule (down-weight or skip names where ma10_slope_5 > 0.05 AND ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct > 0.05) will reduce the false_positive_ruin rate by more than re-weighting toward any single industry.
policy_implications: Remove explicit industry tilts from allocation and replace them with explicit controls on the features that the archaeology actually flags: up_day_ratio_20, vol_ratio_5_20, mom_20, px_vs_ma50, ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct, ma10_slope_5.

Add a momentum-stage filter (penalize or skip when steep ma10_slope_5 is combined with extended ibd_entry_close_vs_trigger_pct) — this directly attacks the largest false_positive_ruin signature without invoking industry.

Tag every pick with snapshot_anon / macro-regime and report performance stratified by regime before reporting industry-stratified performance; if regime explains the spread, industry is a label, not a lever.
Run the matched-pair sector test as the gating diagnostic: do not allocate by industry unless the test shows |t| > 2 stable across at least three non-overlapping time windows.

If industry is retained as a soft prior, cap its weight and require that the industry tilt be justified by a documented, feature-reducible mechanism (e.g., 'biotech systematically shows lower up_day_ratio_20, so we tilt to balance the missing signal') rather than by raw sector return differentials.

UNRESOLVED on whether a residual industry effect exists once features are properly controlled; the frozen evidence does not contain a sector field, so the falsification must be carried out in a downstream diagnostic rather than asserted from this archaeology.
